findings.issue_text: Recovery-code validation in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 accepts codes without atomically consuming them, while getCredentials() reconstructs the complete retained set, allowing successfully used recovery codes to be replayed indefinitely.

goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Recovery-code validation in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 accepts codes without atomically consuming them, while getCredentials() reconstructs the complete retained set, allowing successfully used recovery codes to be replayed indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java, the isValid() method at lines 283-310 validates recovery codes by checking if the input matches any code in the stored list (line 309: `return generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`), but it never removes the used code from storage. The getCredentials() method at lines 227-246 reconstructs the full credential model from the stored data. Since the validation doesn't consume/remove the used code, the same recovery code can be used multiple times, which defeats the purpose of one-time recovery codes. This is a security bug in the test provider implementation.
